Class MKCContainerPanel

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.MKCContainerPanel
public final class MKCContainerPanel extends Object
The one-call, no-mixin registration for a panel whose slots have container parity — they appear, click, and sync on every screen that shows the player inventory (survival, creative, and every chest/furnace/modded container), default-on, opt-out per screen.

What one registration drives

// Consumer COMMON initializer (runs both sides):
MKCContainerPanel.define("inventory-plus:pockets")
    .at(MenuRegion.LEFT_ALIGN_TOP, 7)
    .style(PanelStyle.RAISED)
    .parity(ScreenMatcher.all())                       // default; opt out per screen
    .chrome(() -> List.of(new Button(...)))             // client-only, built lazily
    .addSlot(SlotSpec.at("pockets").count(9)             // slots flow + wrap to width
            .storage(player -> POCKETS.bind(player)))
    .register();
From that single declaration the library:
  1. builds the real, synced MKCSlots on the player's own InventoryMenu (the library-owned MKCInventoryMenuMixin, both sides) — no consumer mixin;
  2. projects the same slots onto every foreign container menu (MKCSlotProjection, both sides);
  3. gets the creative item-picker for free (the existing creative wrapper wraps whatever MKCSlots sit on player.inventoryMenu);
  4. on the client, renders the panel's chrome + slot presentation on every screen the ScreenMatcher accepts (a ScreenPanelAdapter wired via onMatching).

The client/server split this honestly reflects

The server must build a menu's slots at construction time, before any client exists, so the slot data is declared side-neutrally (the SlotSpec recipes) and travels onto every container menu unconditionally — that is the only sync-correct default. The per-screen MKCContainerPanel.Builder.parity(ScreenMatcher) scope therefore gates the client presentation (whether the panel + its slots are drawn and interactive on a given screen), not whether the slot data exists. A slot you opt a screen out of is still present on that menu; it simply isn't shown there. The chrome (MKCContainerPanel.Builder.chrome) is a client-only Supplier so no GUI objects are constructed on a dedicated server.

MKCContainerPanel.Builder.register() is safe to call from the consumer's common initializer: it touches only side-neutral data (recipes, the projection source, the stored definition). The client chrome is materialised later, on the client only, from wireRegisteredChrome() (invoked by MKCClient).

    • address

      public static com.trevorschoeny.menukit.window.Address address(String containerPanelId, String groupId, int localIndex)
      THE canonical Address of one slot created by a container-parity define(...) — use this to name a define()-created slot when arming behavior or reading state by address. Never reconstruct the address by hand.

      Why a dedicated minter: a parity slot does NOT carry the container panel id passed to define(String) as its address panel id — it carries the library-derived id containerPanelId + ":" + groupId (so each group lives in its own collision-free address sub-space). That derivation is an internal rule; this method applies it for you. The raw CreatedSlotAdapter.addressOf encoding is @Internal precisely so a consumer can't hand it the bare define() id and silently mint a non-resolving address — each slot-creation path has its own public minter (MKCContainerPanel.address for parity slots; MKCScreenHandler.address for custom-menu slots). So: 

      // Container-parity slot — derived id applied internally:
Window.slot(MKCContainerPanel.address("inventory-plus:pockets", "pockets", i))
      .set(MKCBehaviorKeys.GATING, gate);

// Custom-menu slot (different path) — bare declared id, its own minter:
Window.slot(MKCScreenHandler.address("inventory-plus:menu:main", "main", i))
      .set(MKCBehaviorKeys.GATING, gate);

      For most consumers the SlotSpec inline verbs (.gate(...), .binding(), .mending(), .quickMove(...)) arm behavior for you and you never call this directly; it remains the explicit seam for by-address arming and for reading per-slot state by address.

      Parameters:
      containerPanelId - the id passed to define(String)
      groupId - the slot group id (the SlotSpec.at(String) group id)
      localIndex - the slot's index within its group

    • wireRegisteredChrome

      @Internal public static void wireRegisteredChrome()
      Builds each registered panel's chrome Panel (chrome elements + auto-generated SlotElements) and wires a ScreenPanelAdapter scoped by the panel's parity matcher. Client-only — invoked once from MKCClient.onInitializeClient, after all consumer common-init register() calls have populated DEFINITIONS (Fabric runs all main entrypoints before any client entrypoint).
